clue.text: Taking picture for retirement

parts.note: with can mean taking, as in tea with sugar, tea taking sugar
a drawing is a picture made with pencil or pen

explanation.surface: Someone receives a framed picture as a leaving present on their last day at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Withdrawing, as a verbal noun, is the act of pulling back or leaving active life, which is what retirement means.

clue.text: Sitting at the traffic lights, spot some drama

parts.note: a driver at a red light is waiting for the signal to go
a spot is a small dot

explanation.surface: A bored driver stuck at red lights notices a bit of street theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Beckett's famous play, in which two tramps wait for someone who never arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Beckett's play is a celebrated example of modern theatre, so it is one piece of drama.

clue.text: Round area providers of hot and cold snacks

indicators.note: round means placed around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: taps supply hot and cold water
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A café's round area serves both hot and cold snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapas are small Spanish dishes, served hot or cold, eaten as bar snacks or appetisers.

clue.text: Loudly announce large contribution to year-end target

indicators.note: a contribution is something put into a whole, so this piece goes inside the other words

parts.note: December, abbreviated, is the end of the year
an aim is a target
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big donation helps a charity hit its target before the year ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim is to speak out in a rhetorical, forceful way, as an orator delivering a speech does.

clue.text: Repeatedly, articles about loaf crusts as fodder

indicators.note: the two articles stand about, around, the crusts of the loaf

parts.note: A is the indefinite article; two of them here

indicators.note: the crusts of a loaf are its outside letters, first and last

parts.note: the word whose outer letters are taken
the crust-and-article pattern is given again, a second LF followed by a closing A

explanation.surface: A note on repeatedly serving up the ends of a loaf, with a couple of articles, as feed for livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: A around LF gives ALFA; 'Repeatedly' runs the crust-then-article pattern once more, so a second LF and a final A follow, sharing the middle article.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne, the plant known as this word, is grown chiefly as animal feed, so it is fodder by example.

clue.text: Inspectors of pub measures said to have teeth

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the phrase is matched by its pronunciation not spelling

parts.note: people who check the measure sizes at an inn would be inn sizers

explanation.surface: Trading-standards officers checking pub measures are reputed to be tough, to have teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To have teeth' in the surface means to have real power; cryptically the teeth are the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Incisors are the sharp cutting front teeth in the mouth, so they are a type of teeth.

clue.text: Unserious proposals that scatter specious glitter

indicators.note: to scatter is to throw things in all directions, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Politicians' flimsy policy ideas sprinkle shallow sparkle around without substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Gesture politics means policies made for show to win approval, without serious intention of achieving real change.

clue.text: Kindles to deposit aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard means on board, so the word for deposit sits inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
to park something is to put it down or deposit it

explanation.surface: E-readers are being loaded on a vessel for delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: Kindles looks like the brand of e-reader, a noun; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To spark a fire or a feeling is to set it going, just as to kindle one is.

clue.text: Request submitted to obtain seal

indicators.note: submitted to suggests being placed into something else, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to get is to obtain
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: An application is formally lodged to secure an official seal of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasket is a shaped ring of rubber or similar material that seals a joint between two surfaces.

clue.text: Sex-obsessed pair taken out and shot

indicators.note: taken out suggests things removed and disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a shot is a photograph, a pic

explanation.surface: A lecherous couple meet a gangland end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken out and shot' reads as an execution, but 'taken out' is the anagram signal and 'shot' is a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: Priapic comes from Priapus, a Greek fertility god with an exaggerated phallus, and means preoccupied with male sexuality.

clue.text: Trouble if such a plant appears

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so the following letters are stirred into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener frets that some unwanted plant may turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuchsia is a flowering shrub with hanging purple and pink blooms, popular in gardens and hanging baskets.

clue.text: Controls big problem with app to be fixed by this

definitions.text: problem with app to be fixed by this

parts.note: reins are what a rider controls a horse with, hence controls
tall means big in height

explanation.surface: An IT helpdesk advises how to put right a major software fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big problem' looks like one phrase, but 'big' belongs to the wordplay and the definition starts at 'problem'.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing and installing software again is the usual remedy offered when a program keeps going wrong.

clue.text: Dope that creates a big stink

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a strong-smelling variety of cannabis
second meaning: a black-and-white animal that sprays a foul smell

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fool causing a fuss; 'stink' is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a potent strain of marijuana and the North American mammal famous for its defensive spray.

clue.text: Green coach losing time

indicators.note: losing means giving something up, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a stagecoach, or stage, was a horse-drawn coach
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An inexperienced sports trainer is running late.
explanation.walkthrough: Green looks like 'inexperienced', but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage green is a soft greyish-green colour named after the herb's leaves, so sage is a shade of green.

clue.text: Injury odd French fellows eventually get

parts.note: impair is the French word for odd, as in an odd number
fellows are men

indicators.note: eventually means in the end, so only the final letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of get

explanation.surface: Strange Frenchmen finally get hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: An impairment is damage or weakening of a body function, the kind of harm that an injury causes.

clue.text: An officer interrupts myself three times when gong is heard

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: me is myself, first time
myself again, as I and then ME, giving the second and third versions
A, plus Lt, the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A military man keeps cutting in while someone talks about themselves at a medal ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Myself three times' means ME, I and ME; the officer goes between the first and the other two.
explanation.definitionFit: In a grand house a gong was struck to summon people to dinner, so it sounds at the hour of eating.

clue.text: History of Gauguin's final piece? Shown to be expert about it

parts.note: proven means shown to be true

indicators.note: about means around, so the expert word wraps the selected letter

parts.note: an ace is an expert

indicators.note: final piece means the very end bit, so only the last letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of Gauguin

explanation.surface: An art specialist confirms a late work by Gauguin, its record traced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to the letter from Gauguin's final piece, which goes inside ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Provenance is the recorded history of ownership of an artwork, proving where it came from.

clue.text: Father Zeus, say, at a temple

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
Zeus is an example of a god, chief of the Greek pantheon

explanation.surface: Father Zeus pictured standing at a temple in ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower built as a Buddhist or Hindu shrine, a kind of sacred building.

clue.text: A name of Scots celebrity

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a Scottish boy's name, a form of Alexander
second meaning: a top-list star, written with a hyphen after the first letter

explanation.walkthrough: Read as A-LISTER, the word is a top celebrity; as one word it is a Scottish first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alister is a Scottish forename, and an A-lister is a celebrity on the top list of invitations.

clue.text: Pupil barrister turning up in case foolishly laughs

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
foolishly suggests something done wrongly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a KC, King's Counsel, is a senior barrister
L is for learner, a pupil

explanation.surface: A trainee lawyer arrives at court and giggles stupidly over a case.
explanation.walkthrough: KC is King's Counsel, a senior British barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: To cackle is to laugh in a loud harsh way, so cackles is a vivid form of laughs.

clue.text: Garment for water sport

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a short-sleeved collared shirt

definitions.note: only the second word: water polo
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the game played on horseback, which also names the pool version

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests swimwear; the answer is both a shirt and the second word of water polo.
explanation.definitionFit: A polo is a short-sleeved knitted shirt, and polo played in a pool by swimmers is water polo.

clue.text: Gong you had responded to

parts.note: an OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a medal or gong
ye'd is an old contraction of ye had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the honour that you once held and replied to.
explanation.walkthrough: A gong is British slang for a medal or honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To have obeyed an order or a call is to have complied with it, that is, responded to it.

clue.text: Enormous number one zero short for writer

indicators.note: short means lacking something, so a letter is missing from the big number

parts.note: a googol is ten to the power of a hundred
a zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A huge figure falls one nought short of what an author needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolai Gogol was a Russian novelist and dramatist, author of Dead Souls and The Government Inspector.

clue.text: Aggressive using handwriting

parts.note: written in a style means using it
cursive is joined-up handwriting

explanation.surface: Someone's script looks angry and forceful.
explanation.definitionFit: Incursive describes making incursions, invasive raids into enemy territory, so it means aggressive or attacking.

clue.text: Run over one day, got into argument

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
Wed is the abbreviation for Wednesday, one day of the week

explanation.surface: A runner, knocked over one day, ended up in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer rhymes with loud, not with code: a row is a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To row, pronounced to rhyme with cow, is to quarrel noisily, so rowed means had a quarrel.

clue.text: Family man is captivated by artist's extremes: one's a shocker

parts.note: a dad is a man in a family

indicators.note: something captivated is held captive, so this word sits inside the outer letters
extremes are the two ends, so only the outer letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of artist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A father is charmed by the edgy work of an artist known for outrageous pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Dada artists set out to shock, with absurd works mocking art itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dadaist belonged to the early twentieth-century anti-art movement that deliberately provoked and scandalised audiences.

clue.text: Humble, grow up in such blocks?

parts.note: low can mean humble in rank
to rise is to grow upward

explanation.surface: A modest person matures living in short buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: such blocks are buildings of only a few storeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-rise describes buildings with few floors, the opposite of high-rise tower blocks.

clue.text: Quality vineyard in depression in these awful religious wars

indicators.note: in puts the first pieces inside the other word
awful suggests something badly made, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
a cru is a high-grade vineyard, as in grand cru
sad means depressed, in low spirits

explanation.surface: A wine estate sits in a hollow amid the horrors of holy war.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' just joins the vineyard to the depression; the second puts both inside the jumbled word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crusades were the medieval Christian military expeditions to recover the Holy Land from Muslim rule.
